title: Pluricentric Standard and Formal Register Across Varieties

sections.content: You know *quienes* from B2 Unit 13, formal written register (*todo aquel que* and *cualquier persona que* with the subjunctive, impersonal *se*, and formal future *deberá*) from B2 Unit 14, and second-person *debes* from B1 Unit 4. At C1, mastering formal Spanish means understanding how a pluricentric standard unites twenty-plus countries without erasing their educated regional varieties.

Modern Spanish has no single 'correct' national accent: the Association of Spanish Language Academies (*las academias*) defines the educated norm as common across the Hispanic world, while recognizing legitimate regional variants (*las variantes*). However, the higher the register rises—in academic essays, legal documents, and international journalism—the more local colloquialisms give way to shared impersonal syntax (*se considera que*, *cabe señalar que*), universal relative clauses (*quienes utilicen*, *cualquier hablante que analice*), and shared syntactic standards. This convergence guarantees mutual intelligibility among more than five hundred million speakers.

sections.title: Colloquial Variety vs. Shared Formal Register
rows: Si hablas con tu acento en otro país, todos te entienden.
Todo aquel que se exprese en su variedad culta será comprendido en cualquier país hispanohablante.
En mi país decimos la palabra así porque nos gusta más.
Se observa que cada comunidad conserva variantes léxicas de pleno prestigio dentro de su norma.
Si quieres consultar una duda, mira el diccionario.
Quienes deseen resolver una duda normativa deberán consultar el diccionario académico.
No hay un español mejor que otro.
Se reconoce hoy que ninguna variedad nacional posee el monopolio del buen uso lingüístico.

items.spanish: Se reconoce en la lingüística actual que el español posee una norma culta compartida por todas las academias.
items.english: It is recognized in current linguistics that Spanish possesses an educated norm shared by all the academies.

items.spanish: Todo aquel que redacte un ensayo académico deberá mantener un registro formal comprensible para cualquier lector hispanohablante.
items.english: Anyone who drafts an academic essay must maintain a formal register understandable to any Spanish-speaking reader.

items.spanish: Quienes estudien la historia de la lengua advertirán que la unidad escrita convive con una gran riqueza de variantes.
items.english: Those who study the history of the language will notice that written unity coexists with a great richness of variants.

items.spanish: Se ruega a los participantes evitar giros excesivamente locales cuando el documento esté destinado a un público internacional.
items.english: Participants are kindly asked to avoid overly local expressions when the document is intended for an international audience.

sections.content: In formal pan-Hispanic prose, remember the agreement rule from B2 Unit 14: impersonal openings with *todo aquel que*, *quienes*, or *cualquier persona que* take the subjunctive when referring to any hypothetical person (*todo aquel que redacte*) and continue in the third person (*deberá*, *su*), never shifting to *tú* (*debes*, *tu*).
